headline: Sony Xperia 5 IV Review: The Compact Flagship That Refuses to Compromise
seo_title: Sony Xperia 5 IV Review: Compact Flagship in Kenya | Affordable Gadgets
seo_description: Is the Sony Xperia 5 IV Kenya's best compact flagship? We review its Zeiss camera, 3.5mm jack, SD card slot & Snapdragon 8 Gen 1. Available at Affordable Gadgets KE.
body_markdown:
## Design and Build: Premium Compact That Fits Your Hand

Out of the box, the Sony Xperia 5 IV makes a statement that big phones aren't the only flagship option. Its 6.1-inch OLED display is wrapped in a slim, flat-edged frame that feels remarkably comfortable in one hand — a rarity in 2026. Sony has retained the IP68 water resistance, Gorilla Glass Victus on both sides, and a textured matte frame that resists fingerprints beautifully.

At just 161g, it's one of the lightest flagships you can buy. And unlike most 2026 phones, it sits flush in a pocket without that awkward protrusion.

## Key Features Under the Hood

Performance is where the Xperia 5 IV punches well above its size. It's equipped with the Snapdragon 8 Gen 1 chipset and 8GB of RAM, making it more than capable of handling heavy multitasking, mobile gaming, and 4K video editing on the go.

Here's a quick look at the standout specs:

- **Camera:** Triple 12MP rear cameras (16mm ultra-wide, 24mm wide, 60mm telephoto) with Zeiss T* coating for exceptional clarity. Every lens can shoot 4K HDR at 120fps.
- **Display:** 6.1-inch FHD+ HDR OLED with 120Hz refresh rate. Sony's BRAVIA HDR remastering makes streaming content look vibrant even under direct Kenyan sunlight.
- **Battery:** 5,000mAh with 30W wired charging, wireless charging, and reverse wireless charging.
- **Storage:** 128GB internal + microSD expansion up to 1TB. Yes, the headphone jack is here too.

## Who Is the Xperia 5 IV Actually For?

The Xperia 5 IV is for anyone who refuses to choose between flagship power and one-handed usability. If you are a photographer who wants manual control over every shot, a commuter who relies on wired headphones, or a traveler who needs expandable storage for offline media, this phone immediately improves your daily workflow.

On the flip side, if you prioritise all-day gaming on the largest possible screen or want the absolute brightest display in direct sunlight, the larger Xperia 1 V or a Galaxy S series may suit you better.

## The Verdict

Sony has done something rare in 2026: they built a true compact flagship that doesn't strip out the features power users actually want. The Xperia 5 IV earns its place as one of the most complete small phones on the market — headphone jack, SD card, wireless charging, IP68, and flagship cameras all in one pocket-friendly package.

Ready to upgrade? Check out the Sony Xperia 5 IV and explore our full range of colours and storage options in the shop today.

headline: Sony Xperia 10 V Review: The World's Lightest 5G Phone With a Monster Battery
seo_title: Sony Xperia 10 V Review: Lightest 5G Phone in Kenya | Affordable Gadgets
seo_description: The Sony Xperia 10 V weighs just 159g yet packs a 5,000mAh battery. Read our full review covering camera, display, and value. Available in Nairobi at Affordable Gadgets KE.
body_markdown:
## Design and Build: Ultra-Light Without the Fragile Feel

At just 159 grams, the Sony Xperia 10 V is officially the world's lightest 5G smartphone. Pick it up and the first thing you notice is how effortlessly it sits in the hand — no wrist fatigue, no awkward balancing act. Yet Sony hasn't sacrificed build quality. The matte plastic back is surprisingly premium, resists fingerprints, and won't shatter if you drop it without a case.

The 6.1-inch OLED display is protected by Gorilla Glass Victus, and the phone carries an IP68 rating, meaning it survives dust and a dip in water. For a mid-range device, that's an exceptional level of durability.

## Key Features Under the Hood

The Xperia 10 V strikes an impressive balance between weight, battery, and everyday performance. It's powered by the Snapdragon 695 chipset with 6GB of RAM — not a gaming powerhouse, but more than adequate for social media, streaming, navigation, and light multitasking.

Here is a quick look at the standout specs:

- **Battery:** 5,000mAh — enormous for a 159g phone. Expect approximately 34 hours of video playback on a single charge. This is the phone's killer feature.
- **Display:** 6.1-inch FHD+ OLED with Triluminos display technology. Sony's expertise in screens (inherited from their TV division) means rich colours and deep blacks.
- **Camera:** Triple rear cameras — 48MP wide, 8MP ultra-wide, and 8MP telephoto. Sony's camera app includes the same manual controls found on the flagship Xperia 1 series.
- **Audio:** Dual front-facing stereo speakers with Sony's audio processing. The 3.5mm headphone jack is present with High-Resolution Audio support.

## Who Is the Xperia 10 V Actually For?

The Xperia 10 V is for anyone who prioritises battery life and portability above all else. If you are a frequent traveller, a student walking between classes, or someone who simply hates carrying a charger, this phone will easily get you through two days of moderate use.

It's also an excellent choice for audiophiles on a budget, thanks to the 3.5mm jack and Hi-Res Audio certification — a rare combination in 2026.

If you need raw gaming performance or the absolute best camera, the Galaxy A series or Pixel 7A may offer better value. But for sheer endurance and pocketability, the Xperia 10 V is unmatched.

## The Verdict

Sony has delivered something genuinely unique: a lightweight, water-resistant 5G phone that never leaves you scrambling for a charger. The Xperia 10 V isn't the flashiest phone on the shelf, but it solves the most common smartphone problem — dead battery — better than almost anything in its class.

Ready to experience two-day battery life? Check out the Sony Xperia 10 V and explore our pricing and stock options today.

## Design and Build: Classic Samsung Elegance

The Samsung Galaxy A42 5G arrives with the refined design language Samsung has perfected across its A-series lineup. The glossy polycarbonate back catches light with a subtle prism effect, while the flat 6.6-inch display keeps bezels minimal. It's not a lightweight at 193g, but the curved edges make it comfortable to hold during long streaming sessions.

Samsung has kept the headphone jack and includes a generous set of sensors including an under-display optical fingerprint reader. The back is a fingerprint magnet, but a case solves that — and Samsung's official cases are widely available.

The Galaxy A42 5G was Samsung's answer to making 5G accessible without breaking the bank. It runs on the Snapdragon 750G chipset — a solid mid-range processor that balances power efficiency with capable everyday performance.

- **Display:** 6.6-inch Super AMOLED with 720 x 1600 resolution. Colours are vibrant and blacks are deep — typical AMOLED excellence. Perfect for Netflix and YouTube.

The Galaxy A42 5G is for anyone looking to future-proof their next phone purchase. If you are a student, first-time smartphone buyer, or someone upgrading from a 4G device, this phone gives you access to 5G networks without requiring a flagship budget.

If you prioritise camera quality above all else, you may want to look at the Pixel 7A. But for a well-rounded Samsung experience with 5G and AMOLED at a reasonable price, the A42 5G delivers.

## The Verdict

The Samsung Galaxy A42 5G remains a compelling choice for anyone wanting to experience 5G, AMOLED, and Samsung's trusted software ecosystem without spending flagship money. The Pixel 7A is powered by Google's custom Tensor G2 chip, the same processor found in the flagship Pixel 7 Pro. If you need the absolute best processor for heavy gaming or want a telephoto zoom lens, the Pixel 7 Pro is a better fit. But for the best camera in the mid-range, the Pixel 7A has no competition.

## The Verdict

The Google Pixel 7A proves that you don't need to spend flagship money to take flagship-quality photos. Between the Tensor G2's AI capabilities, the clean Android experience, and Google's rock-solid update commitment, this phone offers outstanding value. It's not the fastest or the flashiest, but it's arguably the smartest mid-range phone you can buy.

The iPhone 16 is for the vast majority of users who want a modern iPhone experience without paying Pro prices. If you upgrade every 3-4 years, the jump from an iPhone 13 or 14 will feel massive — better cameras, faster performance, USB-C, and the Action Button.

body_markdown:
## Design and Build: The Contour-Cut Revolution

The Galaxy S21 marked a significant design departure for Samsung. The contour-cut camera housing that flows seamlessly into the aluminium frame was instantly iconic and has influenced Samsung's design language ever since. The plastic back (Glasstic) was a controversial choice, but it kept the phone lightweight at 169g and made it more durable against drops.

The flat 6.2-inch Dynamic AMOLED 2X display was a welcome return after the curved displays of previous generations, making screen protectors easy to apply and reducing accidental touches.

## Key Features Under the Hood

body_markdown:
## Design and Build: The Complete Package

The Galaxy S20+ was the Goldilocks phone of Samsung's 2020 lineup — larger than the S20 but not as massive as the S20 Ultra. The 6.7-inch Dynamic AMOLED 2X display with 120Hz refresh rate was stunning, and the glass-metal construction felt premium.

The quad-camera module with a dedicated ToF depth sensor sat in a rectangular housing on the back. The phone weighed 186g, well-balanced for its size.

## Key Features Under the Hood

The Galaxy S20+ offered a complete flagship package for its generation.

Here is a quick look at the standout specs:

- **Display:** 6.7-inch QHD+ Dynamic AMOLED 2X, 120Hz. Large, vibrant, and smooth.
- **Camera:** 12MP main + 64MP telephoto (3x hybrid zoom) + 12MP ultra-wide + ToF depth sensor. The quad-camera system was versatile for any shooting scenario.
- **5G:** Sub-6GHz and mmWave 5G support for future-proof connectivity.
- **Battery:** 4,500mAh with 25W charging. Excellent battery life for a big-screen phone.
- **Storage:** 128GB/256GB/512GB, expandable via microSD.

## The Verdict

The Galaxy S20+ was one of the most well-rounded phones of 2020. The 120Hz display, quad cameras, 5G, and large battery made it a true flagship. In 2026, it's a dated but capable device.

Check out the Samsung Galaxy S20+ in the shop today.
